Roofing Big-Box Retail Along Winston-Salem's Retail Corridors

The retail concentration around Hanes Mall, Stratford Road, and the outparcel developments feeding off those corridors covers a lot of large-format roof area under national chain ownership, regional landlord portfolios, and independent operators. Big-box roofs are structurally simple compared to a hospital or a manufacturing plant, but the procurement standards and scheduling constraints from national retail tenants add their own layer of process.

Large Open-Span Retail Roof Decks

A typical big-box store sits under one open-span low-slope roof with steel bar joist or long-span truss framing and minimal interior columns, which means the roof deck itself usually isn't the limiting factor in a reroof — the wind uplift design and drainage plan are. We run wind uplift calculations to ASCE 7 for the store's exposure category, which in an open-parking-lot retail setting is often more exposed than a downtown building of similar height, and we size the fastening pattern or adhesive bonding accordingly.

Skylights are common on newer big-box construction for daylighting savings, and older stores retrofitted with LED lighting sometimes have skylights that were never properly integrated into the retrofit and are now a documented leak source. We evaluate every skylight separately from the field membrane during inspection, since national retailers often track skylight-related leak claims as a distinct maintenance category.

Retrofit Around Rooftop HVAC and Solar-Ready Curbs

Big-box roofs typically carry several large packaged RTUs serving the sales floor, plus separate units for stockroom and any in-store pharmacy or grocery section. We coordinate RTU curb resets during reroofing with the store's HVAC service contract holder, since national retailers frequently use a dedicated regional HVAC vendor separate from the roofing contractor, and scheduling has to account for both crews being on the roof without conflicting.

  • Wind uplift design run to ASCE 7 for the store's open-lot exposure category
  • Skylight evaluation separate from field membrane inspection
  • RTU curb coordination with the retailer's regional HVAC vendor
  • After-hours scheduling to avoid disrupting store operating hours
  • National account submittal formatting for multi-store retail portfolios
  • Recover feasibility study before committing a store to full tear-off

Scheduling Reroofs Around Retail Operating Hours

Big-box stores rarely close for construction, so tear-off, mechanical fastening, and material staging get scheduled for early morning hours before doors open or overnight where the store's operating model allows it. We coordinate directly with store management on delivery dock access, since roofing material staging can conflict with the store's own freight schedule if it isn't planned around in advance.

Parking lot staging is its own logistics problem at big-box locations, since the same lot serves customer traffic, employee parking, and sometimes an outparcel restaurant or bank with its own lease and access requirements. We fence off a defined staging zone in coordination with the property manager, positioned to avoid peak-hour customer parking counts and any outparcel tenant's dedicated spaces, and we move that zone as the roof project progresses across different sections of the building.

Recover Programs for National Retail Chains

National retail chains managing dozens or hundreds of locations often run a standardized recover or reroof program across their portfolio, with a preferred membrane manufacturer and warranty term set at the corporate level. We work within that standard where a chain has one, rather than proposing an alternate system that doesn't match the retailer's existing portfolio approach, and we flag it clearly when a specific store's condition doesn't fit the standard program — for instance, when wet insulation rules out the recover approach the corporate program assumes.

For independent retail operators without a corporate standard, we run the same recover-versus-replacement analysis we'd run on any commercial building, based on actual moisture testing and deck condition rather than defaulting to the more expensive option.

Procurement Standards Retail REITs Require

Retail properties held by REITs or institutional landlords come with their own procurement documentation requirements, often including standardized bid forms, insurance certificate formats, and a specific warranty term set at the portfolio level. We format submittals to match whatever standard the landlord's asset management team specifies, and we keep a consistent documentation format across multiple stores in the same portfolio so the landlord's team can compare projects side by side.

Insurance certificate requirements at big-box retail properties are often stricter than a typical commercial job, given the value of inventory and fixtures under the roof and the tenant improvement dollars the retailer has invested in the space. We carry coverage limits that match what landlord lease exhibits and REIT vendor programs typically specify, and we provide certificates before mobilization rather than waiting for a request mid-project.

Common Questions From Retail Property Managers

Can roof work happen without closing the store?

Yes, in nearly every case. We schedule tear-off and the noisiest work for before-hours or overnight windows depending on the store's operating schedule.

Do you work within our corporate roofing program's preferred manufacturer?

Yes. Where a national chain has a standardized program, we work within that specification and flag any store-specific condition that doesn't fit the standard assumption.

How do you coordinate with our HVAC vendor during a reroof?

We schedule RTU curb work directly with your regional HVAC contractor so both crews are on the roof at coordinated times rather than working around each other unannounced.

Are skylights inspected as part of a standard roof survey?

We evaluate skylights separately from the field membrane, since they're a common and distinct leak source on big-box stores with older or poorly integrated skylight retrofits.

What documentation format do you use for REIT-owned properties?

We match whatever bid form, insurance certificate, and warranty documentation standard your asset management team specifies, keeping the format consistent across multiple stores in the same portfolio.
